key_insight: Carrier Dynamics by Pockels Imaging (CDPI) directly visualizes internal charge-carrier motion in operative semiconductor devices by mapping local electric-field changes in space and time.
engineering_relevance: This gives device engineers a non-invasive way to connect microscopic carrier transport mechanisms to measurable current, improving diagnosis and design of solar-cell and other optoelectronic devices.
method: Uses Pockels imaging to probe local electric fields inside operating devices
Converts field changes into real-space, time-resolved images of photogenerated carrier clouds
Correlates carrier evolution with conduction and displacement currents
evidence_signal: The abstract reports demonstration in CdTe radiation detectors with micrometre-scale spatial resolution and nanosecond temporal resolution.
watch_item: CDPI depends on a strong electro-optic response, so performance and ease of implementation may be limited in materials or device stacks with weak Pockels sensitivity.
paper_title: Direct Spatiotemporal Imaging of Charge Carrier Dynamics in Operative Semiconductor Devices
